guide.title: About AVI files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVI file?

AVI, short for Audio Video Interleave, is a RIFF container that Microsoft introduced with Windows 3.1 in 1992. Streams inside it are labeled with FOURCC codes, so the .avi extension reveals neither the codec nor the picture quality. Size limits in the first specification are not the ones OpenDML later allowed, which is why a long capture needs software that supports it.

Legacy Windows clips, footage straight from cameras and capture devices, and archives are where AVI shows up. WMV is the target when an older Windows workflow expects Windows Media Video.

### Programs that open AVI files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFplay, FFmpeg's own player, plays AVI, and mpv offers desktop playback.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere on both can import AVI, provided it has a decoder for what the file holds.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android is a free player, though what it can show hinges on the streams within the file, and VLC for iOS handles most movie formats along with local and network media.

### AVI and WMV compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .avi with video/x-msvideo; .wmv with video/x-ms-wmv, a label the Library of Congress records as commonly used, not an IANA registration.
- **Container**: AVI is a RIFF container able to wrap many different codecs. A .wmv file uses Microsoft's ASF container with Windows Media coded content.
- **Typical use**: AVI is found in legacy Windows clips and archived footage. WMV carried older Windows video, screencasts and Windows Media broadcasts.

Here FFmpeg decodes the AVI and writes a new WMV. It deinterlaces the picture, scales the longer side to at most 1920 px with even dimensions, and caps the frame rate at 30 fps. The audio is re-encoded as well, so nothing is copied across untouched. The command names no codec, so FFmpeg's defaults decide, and a detailed picture can come out soft.

### Other ways to convert AVI to WMV

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i capture.avi -c:v wmv2 -c:a wmav2 archive.wmv` to pick FFmpeg's Windows Media Video and Windows Media Audio encoders yourself. This re-encodes both streams.

### Problems with AVI files

A black picture with working sound means the player lacks the video codec; the file is not empty. Opening it in a second player with its own decoders tells you which case you have.

Aspect ratio and scan type are recorded inconsistently across AVI implementations. A picture that looks stretched or combed in one player may look right in another, so judge the WMV in the same player you used for the AVI.

guide.title: About BMP files
guide.markdown:
### What is a BMP file?

BMP is a raster image family that Microsoft controls, first seen on Windows and OS/2. Version 5 of the format shipped with Windows 98 in 1998 and added an ICC profile plus an alpha channel. Pixels are commonly stored uncompressed, though lossless compression exists. It is registered as image/bmp.

Windows screen captures and system graphics are where BMP is commonly encountered.

### Programs that open BMP files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick reads BMP images. XnView MP also lists BMP among its supported formats; company use requires a license.
- **Web:** Mozilla Firefox displays BMP pictures in browser content, and Google Chrome is listed as supporting BMP in Mozilla's compatibility data.

### BMP and ICO compared

- **Names and media types**: .bmp with image/bmp; .ico with image/vnd.microsoft.icon.
- **What each holds**: a BMP is one picture. An ICO file can bundle several images and stores its numbers little-endian.
- **Where ICO is used**: Microsoft's graphical interface icons and website favicons. Windows Vista icon guidance adds a larger image for high-DPI displays.

The ICO written here has one image only, and ImageMagick writes it from the decoded pixels. When the BMP is taller or wider than 256 px, it is fitted inside a square of that size with its proportions kept; a smaller one is left at its own size and not enlarged. A full-size image is stored as PNG data inside the ICO. The color profile and other metadata are dropped.

### Other ways to convert BMP to ICO

- **Pillow:** `Image.open("badge.bmp").save("badge.ico", sizes=[(16,16),(32,32),(48,48),(256,256)])` builds a multi-size icon in Python. Pillow ignores any size bigger than the original image.

### Problems with BMP files

Editable vector shapes and live type do not survive in a BMP, so thin strokes and small lettering that read well in a large preview can disappear when the picture is shrunk to icon size. Look at the icon at the size people will see.

Stretch a small icon over a high-DPI screen and it looks soft. Start from the largest clean picture you have, because a smaller bitmap is left at its size rather than scaled up.

An uncompressed BMP can also be bulky, so PNG or JPEG may be more practical when the picture is only being shared.

guide.title: About FLV files
guide.markdown:
### What is an FLV file?

FLV is a binary format associated with Macromedia Flash video delivery. FLV allows no more than one picture track and one sound track. Pictures use Sorenson or On2 VP6, sound uses MP3, PCM or ADPCM. ActionScript in a Flash SWF could point to a separate FLV file. Adobe ended Flash Player support on 31 December 2020, yet saved lectures and downloaded clips still sit around as FLV files.

### Programs that open FLV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player lists FLV input along with Sorenson and VP6-family decoding, and FFplay uses FFmpeg decoders for FLV.
- **Mobile:** Android gets the desktop player's decoding features through VLC for Android, while VLC for iOS bypasses the system player for local files.

### FLV and AVI compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .flv; .avi, which goes with video/x-msvideo.
- **Container**: FLV was built for Flash delivery and carries a single video and a single audio stream. AVI is a RIFF file that Microsoft introduced in 1992 to interleave video and audio.
- **Codecs**: an AVI may hold raw, lossless or lossy pictures, which is why the extension never reveals what a player must decode.

The output is MPEG-4 video tagged Xvid with no B-frames, plus MP3 audio at 96 kbps. Interlaced frames are cleaned up, any side over 1920 px is shrunk to fit with even dimensions, and 30 fps is the ceiling. Everything runs in your browser, and your file stays on your device.

### Other ways to convert FLV to AVI

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i lecture.flv -c:v mpeg4 -q:v 4 -c:a libmp3lame lecture.avi` to choose the quality scale yourself. It re-encodes both streams.

### Problems with FLV files

Adobe retired Flash Player, so hunting for a copy of it will not help with an old FLV. Use a player that ships decoders of its own, such as VLC.

The FLV extension does not identify a single video codec; a reader also needs the decoder for the stream. A player that opens the file but shows no picture is missing that decoder.

FLV offers one audio stream, so alternative language tracks have nowhere to go inside it.

When the AVI is ready, watch for lip-sync drift and readable screen text, and keep the FLV until you have checked.

guide.title: About GIF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a GIF file?

GIF is an indexed-color raster format that supports both individual pictures and timed image sequences. Every picture in a GIF draws from a palette limited to 256 entries, and transparency works by flagging one entry as clear, so soft edges cannot keep partial opacity. That suits flat logos and badges better than photographs.

For an icon, the real question is which frame carries the drawing.

### Programs that open GIF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP can export a single picture or a multilayer animation as GIF, and ImageMagick reads GIF, though your install's own format list is the final word on support.
- **Web:** Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox display GIF files in the page.
- **Mobile:** Safari shows GIF files, as does Chrome on a phone.

### GIF and ICO compared

- **Names and media types**: .gif and .ico; the registered media type for ICO is image/vnd.microsoft.icon.
- **Content**: a GIF is a palette-based sequence of frames. ICO files may include several pictures and are little-endian.
- **Typical use**: ICO is Microsoft's format for interface icons, and it is widely associated with website favicons.

The page decodes the GIF to pixels and keeps its first frame; delays and looping are not carried over. An image taller or wider than 256 px is shrunk to fit a 256 by 256 square with its shape unchanged, a smaller one stays as it is, and a full-size image goes into the ICO as PNG data. Metadata is dropped.

### Other ways to convert GIF to ICO

- **Pillow:** `Image.open("reaction.gif").save("reaction.ico", sizes=[(16,16),(32,32),(48,48)])` writes several sizes from one frame. The GIF loader supports seek() and tell(), so you can move to another frame before saving.

### Problems with GIF files

GIMP caps GIF exports at a 256-color palette, and gradients may shift as a result; the banding shows up once the picture is small. Look at the result on both light and dark backgrounds at its real size.

High-DPI screens show a small icon blurry, so prepare the largest clean still you have.

Because the output holds one image, prepare the version you want as a still first. A small logo or badge converts best; an animated reaction rarely makes a readable icon.

guide.title: About JPEG files
guide.markdown:
### What is a JPEG file?

JPEG is a lossy raster format from the Joint Photographic Experts Group committee. It suits photographs, and the .jpg and .jpeg endings mean the same thing. It has no alpha transparency and stores a grid of pixels, so camera output, web photographs and email attachments are typical JPEGs.

A JPEG of a logo shows the shapes but holds none of the paths or type that drew them.

### Programs that open JPEG files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP opens JPEG files for editing; ImageMagick also reads them, but support depends on how your copy was built.
- **Web:** Browsers such as Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox show JPG images directly.
- **Mobile:** Safari and Chrome show them on a phone.

### JPEG and AI compared

- **Extensions**: .jpg or .jpeg on one side, .ai on the other.
- **Contents**: a JPEG is flat pixels. An AI is Adobe Illustrator's native artwork format, where vector objects and placed pixel pictures can share one document.
- **History**: PostScript underlay AI files until Illustrator 9 reworked the format in 2000. Newer files can also include a PDF rendition alongside the Illustrator data.

The AI written here is a PDF made in your browser, with a PNG copy of your picture placed on a page the size of its pixels. It carries no Illustrator data and nothing is traced, so the picture remains pixels and has no editable paths. The JPEG is not uploaded.

### Other ways to convert JPEG to AI

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick photo.jpg photo.ai`. ImageMagick's format list shows both JPEG and AI as readable and writable.

### Problems with JPEG files

Transparent pixels cannot survive JPEG export, so a logo saved as a JPEG sits on a solid background, and that background goes into the AI file too.

A JPEG keeps no editable layer stack. Retain the project file or the original vector artwork when you have one, because nothing in the JPEG can bring it back.

Two editors given an identical quality number may compress differently, so two JPEGs of one logo can look unlike. If the AI file is for print or packaging, start from the original artwork rather than from a picture that already lost detail.

guide.title: About M4A files
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4A file?

An M4A is MPEG-4 audio on its own, with no picture track. Inside you normally find AAC sound or lossless ALAC, plus tags and artwork. Songs from Apple's music apps, podcasts and iPhone voice memos are common examples. The extension alone does not establish quality, because the same .m4a ending covers both lossy and lossless sound.

### Programs that open M4A files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity imports M4A through its optional FFmpeg library and skips protected files, and FFplay plays the container.
- **Web:** Firefox plays supported media directly, with AAC availability depending on system codecs, while Chrome plays supported MP4 audio and the codec inside still matters.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android is free and decodes whatever the container holds, and so does the mpv port for Android, which the mpv project links to.

### M4A and AIFF compared

- **Names and media types**: .m4a; .aiff with audio/aiff and audio/x-aiff.
- **Origin**: Apple created AIFF as a relative of the IFF wrapper family from Electronic Arts. Its specification is dated 4 January 1989.
- **Compression**: M4A is usually lossy AAC, or lossless ALAC. AIFF often carries uncompressed linear PCM, and AIFF-C extends the family to compressed audio.

The page decodes the M4A and writes 16-bit big-endian PCM, dropping any video stream. FFmpeg runs inside your browser as WebAssembly, so the audio is not uploaded, and a long recording simply takes longer on a slower device.

### Other ways to convert M4A to AIFF

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i interview.m4a -vn -c:a pcm_s24be interview.aiff` for 24-bit audio. It decodes the same way but keeps more bits per sample, and it cannot restore detail the M4A already lost.

### Problems with M4A files

Audacity cannot read M4A until its optional FFmpeg library is installed, and protected recordings are refused on that route. Opening several recordings in a single Audacity window leaves the project with the last file's tags.

A very large AIFF is expected here. If you need only part of a recording, trim it in an editor before exporting.

Listen for clipping and compare the length of the new AIFF with the original.

faqs.answer: No. The opus-tools encoder reads Wave, AIFF, FLAC, Ogg FLAC or raw PCM input, so the MP4 has to be turned into one of those first.

guide.title: About MP4 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 is the MPEG-4 container, which can hold several kinds of track side by side. The extension does not say which codecs are inside, so one MP4 may carry H.264 and AAC while another has no sound at all. For pulling out audio, the thing that matters is whether a soundtrack exists.

An MP4 stores its index data in one place, so a recording that was interrupted midway may not play at all.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** mpv plays MP4 on the desktop, and FFplay plays it.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports the container when the necessary decoder is available.
- **Web:** Firefox plays supported media directly and may rely on system codecs for AAC and H.264, and Chrome plays supported combinations where the internal codec still matters.
- **Mobile:** The VLC apps on Android and iPhone cost nothing; whether a file plays hinges on the streams inside.

### MP4 and Opus compared

- **Names**: .mp4; .opus, which commonly holds Opus audio in an Ogg stream as specified in RFC 7845.
- **Standards**: RFC 6716 from the IETF, dated September 2012, defines Opus, which merges Skype's SILK with Xiph.Org's CELT.
- **Contents**: MP4 carries picture and sound. Opus is lossy audio only, designed for speech and music.

The page drops the video and encodes the audio with libopus at 128 kbps. FFmpeg runs inside your browser, so the MP4 is not uploaded.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to Opus

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i talk.mp4 -vn -c:a libopus -b:a 96k talk.opus` to choose your own bitrate.
- **Audacity:** open the MP4, which needs the optional FFmpeg library, then choose File > Export Audio (Ctrl+Shift+E) and pick Opus.
- **opus-tools with FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i session.mp4 -vn session.wav`, then `opusenc --bitrate 64 session.wav session.opus`.

### Problems with MP4 files

Playing the container is not the same as decoding what it holds, so a player can open an MP4 yet lack the codec for its sound. A clip recorded without sound gives an editor no audio track to work with.

Reading Vorbis from Ogg is no proof that a program decodes Opus, since the Ogg mapping uses distinct Opus headers. If a player rejects the file, try another one before blaming the conversion.

Afterward, listen to the result at dialogue breaks and music transitions.

guide.title: About MPG files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MPG file?

MPG is a suffix for MPEG video; the .mpeg and .mpg endings are both used. The MPEG-2 standard was written for broadcasting compressed TV pictures, and DVDs adopted it afterward. In MPEG systems, picture, sound and data are coded and carried as streams. The Library of Congress records video/mpeg as the media type.

Some files are system streams and others raw video, so knowing which you have helps pick the right demuxer.

### Programs that open MPG files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC accepts MPEG elementary, program and transport streams as input; FFplay uses FFmpeg's decoders.
- **Mobile:** Phones are covered by VLC for Android, which reuses the desktop decoding, and by VLC for iOS for local movies.

### MPG and AVI compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mpg with video/mpeg; .avi with video/x-msvideo.
- **Container**: an MPEG file organizes coded picture and sound as streams. AVI is a RIFF container that Microsoft introduced in 1992.
- **Codecs**: playback needs the audio decoder as well as the video one, and sharing a file does not make the two codecs interchangeable.

The AVI carries Xvid-tagged MPEG-4 video with no B-frames and MP3 sound at 96 kbps. Interlaced frames are deinterlaced, the longer side is fitted to 1920 px where needed with even dimensions, and the frame rate tops out at 30 fps. FFmpeg runs inside your browser, so the MPG is not uploaded. Several files are converted one after another, and each downloads as its own AVI.

### Other ways to convert MPG to AVI

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i broadcast.mpg -c:a libmp3lame -c:v mpeg4 -q:v 3 broadcast.avi` for a different quality setting. It re-encodes rather than copying streams.

### Problems with MPG files

MPEG compression is lossy and drops detail from the source picture; encoding a second time drops more. Keep the MPG until you have checked the AVI.

Comb lines and a stretched picture are easy to mistake for damage. Aspect ratio and scan type are not handled consistently across video file formats, so compare a moving scene with the MPG in the same player before blaming the conversion.

A player that opens the AVI but shows no picture or plays no sound lacks one of the decoders; VLC is a quick way to tell.

faqs.question: Is an MXF file a video codec?
faqs.answer: No. MXF, SMPTE's Material Exchange Format, is a wrapper for essence plus metadata, and the video inside can use different codecs. A camera MXF and a broadcast MXF may need different decoders.

faqs.question: Will the MOV be a ProRes master?
faqs.answer: No. The result is a speed-first H.264 encode with AAC audio, which makes a review copy, not an editing master.

faqs.question: Is the MOV the same quality as the MXF?
faqs.answer: No. The picture is compressed again with a lossy, speed-first setting, so detail is lost. Keep the MXF as your source.

faqs.question: Does a 4K MXF stay at full size and frame rate?
faqs.answer: No. A 4K clip is shrunk until its longer side is 1920 px, and frames beyond 30 per second are dropped without shortening the clip. Clips already smaller keep their dimensions, less a pixel when a side is odd.

faqs.question: Does the MOV keep the MXF's metadata?
faqs.answer: Global tags like a title come across when the MOV has matching fields. The video and audio inside are new encodes, and changing the wrapper does not guarantee that specialized metadata or ancillary streams are retained.

faqs.question: Why does my MXF look incomplete on its own?
faqs.answer: A lone copy can be missing material, because certain MXF layouts keep essence outside the file. Keep the camera card's folder structure together.

faqs.question: Does the MOV start playing before it finishes downloading?
faqs.answer: The converter moves the index to the beginning of the file with FFmpeg's fast start option, which is meant to let a player begin early when the MOV is served over the web.

faqs.question: Can I queue several MXF files?
faqs.answer: Yes. Clips go through one at a time, each MOV downloads separately and no archive is built.

guide.title: About MXF files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MXF file?

MXF is the Material Exchange Format, standardized through SMPTE documents. Media essence and descriptive or structural metadata are packaged together in it, and professional acquisition, exchange and preservation workflows use it. Files end in .mxf and the media type is application/mxf.

Operational patterns set out how packages and essence are arranged, and certain layouts point to essence kept elsewhere. A lone clip may therefore be incomplete without the files around it.

### Programs that open MXF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player lists MXF input, and FFmpeg reads MXF essence. Some MXF files may still require a professional application, because not every essence structure is arranged for ordinary playback.

### MXF and MOV compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mxf with application/mxf; .mov with video/quicktime, and QuickTime files may also use .qt.
- **Origin**: Apple introduced QuickTime's MOV format in 1991, and Windows got it in 1994. It is built from objects called atoms.
- **Purpose**: MXF is built for production exchange. MOV picture tracks include H.264, ProRes and Motion JPEG, and sound is often AAC or raw PCM.

The MOV holds H.264 video at CRF 32 with an ultrafast preset, AAC audio at 96 kbps and a fast-start index. A longer side over 1920 px is shrunk, and 30 fps is the most it will keep. It is a review copy rather than a master. FFmpeg runs inside your browser, so the MXF is not uploaded, and the clip you chose stays unchanged on your device.

### Other ways to convert MXF to MOV

- **FFmpeg stream copy:** run `ffmpeg -i camera.mxf -c copy rewrap.mov` to copy the streams without decoding or encoding. It works only when the MOV container accepts the codecs inside the MXF.
- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i camera.mxf -c:v prores_ks -profile:v 2 -c:a pcm_s16le edit.mov` to encode ProRes video and PCM audio instead.

### Problems with MXF files

A clip that opens in one tool but not another often depends on a missing companion file or an essence codec the tool lacks. Keep the whole folder from the camera card.

A QuickTime file can use a codec your editor lacks. Changing the ending of a file name does not re-encode its video or add a missing decoder.

The MOV is compressed again with a speed-first setting, so treat it as a copy. Use the MOV to review or share a rough cut, and go back to the MXF for color work and the final export.
